samples.summary: The "dark launch" is not one: on the shipped 0.7.22 pin every document publishes the `unsupported` lapse, so every user's `Not saved` tooltip now blames their browser for our dependency pin
samples.evidence:
`packages/frontend/package.json:66` pins `@yorkie-js/react` to `0.7.22`, and `yorkie-capabilities.ts` sets `MinClientKeyVersion = "0.7.23"`, so `supportsClientKey()` is false for every render today. The lapse is computed at `collab-document-provider.tsx:291-299` as `decided?.durable ? undefined : !supportsClientKey() ? "unsupported" : …`, and `DurabilityLapseScope` wraps BOTH branches (lines ~340+), i.e. it is published for every collaborative document, durable or not. `sync-status-tooltip.ts` LAPSE_REASONS maps `unsupported` → "This browser cannot save documents locally." and `tooltipFor`'s `not-saved` arm appends it unconditionally (`const why_not = lapse ? ...`).

Net effect on the current pin: 100% of users — nobody has opted in, nobody can — who go offline with unsent edits see a tooltip asserting a false thing about their browser. The design's Rollout section stakes the whole staging argument on "nothing changes for anyone until they opt in" (offline-local-persistence.md § Rollout), and sync-status.md's central risk is "the chip could imply durability it does not have" — this is the mirror of that risk: the chip now mis-attributes the absence of durability. Either gate the lapse scope on the feature being reachable, or give the version-pin case wording that does not accuse the user's browser.

samples.summary: Housekeeping and the two access-revocation purges run unconditionally, so users who never opt in do pay for the feature — contradicting the design's own "pay nothing" / dark-launch framing
samples.evidence:
`OfflineRuntime` is mounted from `PrivateRoute` for every signed-in user and gates on neither `getOfflinePersistenceEnabled()` nor `supportsClientKey()` (grep for both across `packages/frontend/src` returns no hit in `offline-runtime.tsx` or `api/workspaces.ts`). Every session therefore opens a `WafflebaseDocStore`, runs `retryPendingOfflineErase`, `collectStale`, and an extra `GET /documents` feeding `purgeRevokedOfflineDocuments`. `deleteWorkspace`/`removeMember` additionally issue `fetchWorkspace` + `fetchDocuments` before every workspace delete and member removal (`api/workspaces.ts` `documentIdsIn`), again for everybody.

The design states the opposite as a property: "Users who never opt in pay nothing for this feature existing" (§ Turning it on) and "PR 4 is a dark launch: nothing changes for anyone until they opt in" (§ Rollout). Some unconditional cleanup is legitimate (a user who opted in and then out must still be swept), but that could be gated on anything actually being stored rather than paid by every session and every destructive workspace action.

samples.summary: The design doc and the README entry both claim the offline-copy recovery reuses the existing copy engine; it reuses the import engine instead
samples.evidence:
offline-local-persistence.md § Losing work anyway: "we already have the machinery for it in `DocumentCopyService` / `POST /documents/:id/copy`", and See Also lists "document-copy.md — the copy engine the offline-copy recovery path reuses". The README entry added in this diff repeats it: "returns unreconcilable `LocalChangesDropped` work as a `(offline copy)` document … over the existing copy engine".

`lib/offline-copy-recovery.ts` calls neither. It uses `createWorkspaceDocument` + `applyImportedContent` (the Miro/file *import* path) and, for notes, its own `writeNote`. Nothing in the diff references `copyDocument` or `POST /documents/:id/copy`. The choice is defensible — the source content is local bytes the server does not have, so the copy endpoint cannot serve it — but the doc asserts a reuse relationship that does not exist, which is exactly what the design-doc-per-subsystem discipline is meant to prevent a reader from having to discover by grep.

samples.summary: Near-verbatim duplicate of `date-format-preference.ts` (storage + session-mirror + dual-event pattern), and the two already give different answers
samples.evidence:
`lib/date-format-preference.ts` (95 lines) and the new `lib/offline-persistence-preference.ts` (121 lines) are the same module with the value type swapped: same `STORAGE_KEY`/`CHANGE_EVENT` pair, same `memoryX` mirror with the same multi-line comment about QuotaExceededError vs SecurityError, same `subscribe`, same `useSyncExternalStore` shape. The design endorses "built on `lib/date-format-preference.ts`'s shape" — the shape, not a second copy of the code.

They have already diverged in the way duplicated logic does: the new file adds a module-scope `storage` listener that clears the mirror when another tab writes the key (lines ~100-110), which `date-format-preference.ts` lacks. So on a failed write followed by a cross-tab change, the two preferences now behave differently for no reason a reader can discover. A `createLocalPreference<T>(key, default, parse)` in `lib/` would serve both and is the reuse this repo expects.
searchedFor: glob packages/frontend/src/lib/*.ts for an existing preference factory

samples.summary: `writeNote` re-implements `applyImportedContent`'s Yorkie client lifecycle rather than extending `ImportedContent` with a `note` arm
samples.evidence:
`apply-imported-content.ts:228-310` already owns "construct a `Client`, `activate()` outside the try, `attach` with the type's `initialRoot`, write, `detach`, `deactivate` in `finally`" for sheet/doc/slides/board, with commentary explaining each ordering decision. `offline-copy-recovery.ts`'s `writeNote` reproduces that whole lifecycle (its own comment even says it "Mirrors `applyImportedContent`'s own lifecycle") because `ImportedContent` has no `note` variant.

`ImportedContent`'s doc comment states exactly why PDF is absent, which marks the union as the intended extension point; adding `{ type: "note"; markdown: string }` there would have kept one owner of the client lifecycle. As written, a future fix to attach/detach handling has two places to land and will get one.
searchedFor: read of apply-imported-content.ts header and ImportedContent union

samples.summary: Stated Goals are unmet on the shipped dependency pin, and the only remaining action is outside this PR
samples.evidence: The doc's Goals lead with "Edits made while disconnected survive a reload or a browser crash … on a device where the user has asked for it." With `@yorkie-js/react` pinned at 0.7.22 (`packages/frontend/package.json:66`) and `MinClientKeyVersion = "0.7.23"`, `supportsClientKey()` is false, so both opt-in entry points are hidden and `useDurableDocument` refuses every document. The doc is candid about this ("PR 4 lands inert, and stays inert until one upstream release … the Goals at the top of this document are unmet until the dependency is bumped"), so this is disclosed rather than hidden — but it is the spec-conformance state of the branch and should be weighed when deciding to merge: what is verifiable here is the wiring, not the outcome, and the 0.7.23 release does not exist yet at the time of writing per the doc's own note.

samples.summary: The chip-reason table maps "IndexedDB unavailable (private browsing)" to "This browser cannot save locally", but the code reaches that string only through the SDK version gate
samples.evidence: § What the user sees lists a row "IndexedDB unavailable (private browsing) | false | This browser cannot save locally". In the implementation the `unsupported` lapse — whose text is "This browser cannot save documents locally." — is produced solely by `!supportsClientKey()` (`collab-document-provider.tsx:293`). A store that cannot open in private browsing surfaces through `onWriteFailure` as `write-failed`, i.e. "This device could not be written to." The documented row and the shipped wording therefore do not correspond; harmless behaviourally, but the doc is the reference for these strings.

samples.summary: A vitest-importing suite lives in a production source path without a `.test` suffix
samples.evidence: `src/lib/doc-store-contract.ts` imports `describe/it/expect` from vitest and is the only non-`.test.*` file under `packages/frontend/src` that does (grep for `from "vitest"` across `src`). It is excluded from the vitest `include` globs in `vite.config.ts` (`**/*.test.ts`), so it runs only via its importer and is never bundled — but placing shared test scaffolding under `src/lib/` beside shipped modules is a layering oddity; `src/lib/__tests__/` or a `.testkit.ts` suffix would say what it is.

samples.summary: `keepArchives` is a configuration option no caller uses, left over from a design decision that was reversed
samples.evidence: `eraseOfflineData(store, userId, { keepArchives })` forwards to `dropAllForUser`, whose comment says the flag exists "for the one caller that did not ask for any of this: a session the server expired". That caller was removed by this same change — the design now states the 401 path erases nothing at all — so no call site passes it. knip does not see unused option fields, so nothing else will flag it.

samples.summary: Unrelated quote-style churn mixed into the change, and inconsistent quoting among the new files
samples.evidence: `src/lib/utils.ts`, `vite.config.ts` and `components/__tests__/collab-document-provider.test.tsx` are reformatted double-quote→single-quote wholesale with no functional change, enlarging the diff of an already very large PR. Meanwhile the new files disagree with each other: `durable-session.ts`, `wafflebase-doc-store.ts`, `offline-erase.ts` use double quotes while `collab-document-provider.tsx`, `durable-yorkie-provider.tsx`, `offline-runtime.tsx` use single. Prettier is write-only here and no lane checks formatting, so nothing will reconcile this.

verdict.reason: Every element of the claim checks out in the tree. package.json:66 pins @yorkie-js/react to 0.7.22 and vite.config.ts:414-418 injects that pin as __YORKIE_REACT_VERSION__, while yorkie-capabilities.ts:24 requires 0.7.23 — so supportsClientKey() is false on every shipped render (the design itself says so at offline-local-persistence.md:612-622). collab-document-provider.tsx:291-299 therefore computes lapse === "unsupported" for every document, and the return at 349-373 wraps BOTH branches in DurabilityLapseScope, so it is published above every collaborative editor. The chip is inside that scope on the real routes (notes-detail.tsx:379-394 -> SiteHeader syncStatus at site-header.tsx:108), reads it at sync-status-chip.tsx:79 and passes it to tooltipFor at line 322, where sync-status-tooltip.ts:111-112 appends LAPSE_REASONS.unsupported = "This browser cannot save documents locally." (line 30) unconditionally in the not-saved arm. No guard makes this unreachable: only the *offer* is gated on supportsClientKey() (sync-status-chip.tsx:95-99), not the lapse publication — even though yorkie-capabilities.ts:69-75 states every surface must go behind the gate. Design fit is genuinely violated: the design's tooltip table (offline-local-persistence.md:516-524) assigns that sentence to the IndexedDB-unavailable row, not to the version pin (durable-document-context.ts:105-106 defines "unsupported" as the pinned React package lacking clientKey), and the Rollout section (lines 597-599) stakes the dark launch on "nothing changes for anyone until they opt in". The cost is outside codebase tidiness — every user who goes offline with unsent edits is told something false about their browser — which is major under this lens.
